title: Define fixture-backed API boundary and SiteFlow state contracts
objective: Create the typed SiteFlow read models, fixture-backed client, polling/state helpers, and redaction guardrails that all views consume until a real control-plane API exists.
actions: Define domain enums and types for Project, RepositoryBinding, SourceEvent, BuildJob, BuildEvent, Artifact, Deployment, ReleaseChannel, PreviewDeployment, RouteRevision, CdnOperation, ChannelEvent, AuditEvent, SafetyCheck, and LogChunk.
Define read models for project list, project detail, deployment detail, release candidate, rollback target list, command result, route revision evidence, and global summary.

Create a SiteFlowClient interface with methods for listing projects, reading project detail, reading deployment detail, reading release console state, reading rollback console state, promoting deployment, rolling back deployment, polling active operation state, and reading log chunks.

Implement FixtureSiteFlowClient with deterministic fixtures covering healthy, queued, running, failed, route-drift, route-pending, route-failed, CDN-disabled, CDN-failed, rollback-ineligible, stale-candidate, and empty states.
Create async state and polling helpers that can support snapshot reads now and SSE/short-poll replacement later without changing page components.
Create redaction helpers for secrets, provider payloads, manifests, route config, and logs; fixtures may include internal canary values only if tests prove they are never rendered raw.
Document in code-level type names that the database read model is the UI source of truth and artifact storage owns immutable bytes only.

files.purpose: client interface and command payload contracts
read model fixture data and scenario helpers
contract, status, polling, and redaction tests

new_tests: FixtureSiteFlowClient returns complete read models for all five target route families.
Status helpers keep deployment success, artifact verification, route revision, and CDN operation states distinct.
Promotion and rollback command payloads require actor, reason, channel, target deployment, and idempotency key.
Redaction helpers remove secret canary values from project settings, logs, manifests, route config, and provider payloads.

criteria: src/lib/api/siteflowClient.ts exports an interface named SiteFlowClient with listProjects, getProject, getDeployment, getReleaseConsole, getRollbackConsole, promoteDeployment, rollbackDeployment, pollOperation, and getLogChunk methods.
src/domain/siteflow.ts contains the domain names SourceEvent, BuildJob, Artifact, Deployment, ReleaseChannel, RouteRevision, ChannelEvent, and AuditEvent.
src/lib/fixtures/siteflow.fixtures.ts contains scenarios for healthy, queued, routeDrift, routePending, routeFailed, cdnDisabled, rollbackIneligible, staleCandidate, and emptyProjects.
src/lib/redaction.test.ts proves a fixture secret canary string does not survive redaction.
npm test -- --run src/lib src/domain and npm run build pass.

risks: If read models are too UI-specific, future backend integration may require broad rewrites; keep the client boundary explicit.
If fixtures omit failure and stale states, feature pages may accidentally assume only healthy deployments.
Secrets must be redacted centrally rather than ad hoc inside individual page components.
